title: Prompting & Structured Outputs
summary: A language model produces text. Your program needs data. This module closes that gap reliably, not with a nicer-sounding prompt, but with validation and repair logic that doesn’t trust the model to behave.
objectives: Turn free-text model output into a typed object your code can trust
Write a schema the model can follow and your code can enforce
Catch parse errors and validation errors separately
Repair bad output once, with the exact error fed back
Decide when to fail loudly instead of guessing
Explain what native structured outputs do and don’t guarantee

lessons.title: Asking for structure: schemas in the prompt
Native structured outputs and JSON mode

exercise.title: Make parse_ticket() safe
exercise.prompt: The model returns a ticket as text. Turn it into a validated Ticket, and when it can’t be trusted, raise a clear ValueError instead of crashing somewhere downstream.
exercise.header:
import json
from typing import Literal
from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError

class Ticket(BaseModel):
    intent: Literal["refund", "billing", "bug", "other"]
    order_id: int | None
    urgency: Literal["low", "medium", "high"]
exercise.hint: Models often wrap JSON in ```json fences. Strip them first, then use Ticket.model_validate_json() and convert ValidationError into the ValueError your caller expects.

questions.question: Your code needs {"intent": …, "order_id": …} from a model. What makes that reliable?
options: A firmer prompt: “Return ONLY valid JSON.”
Parsing and validating against a schema, then repairing or failing on a mismatch
questions.explanation: Prompting lowers the failure rate; it never removes it. Reliability comes from code that checks every response.

questions.question: The model returns valid JSON, but "intent": "refund_request". Your schema allows refund, billing, bug, other. What kind of failure is this?
questions.explanation: It parsed fine, so it isn’t a syntax problem. The value is outside the enum, which is exactly what validation exists to catch.

questions.question: What should a repair attempt send back to the model?
options: The invalid output plus the specific validation error
Nothing, just retry at a higher temperature
questions.explanation: The error message tells the model precisely what to fix. Retrying blind just rolls the dice again.

questions.question: One repair attempt still fails validation. What’s the right move?
options: Fail loudly: raise, log the raw output, route to a fallback
Return a partial object with default values
questions.explanation: Unbounded retries burn time and money. A loud, logged failure is something you can see, count and fix.

questions.question: Native structured outputs (constrained decoding) guarantee that…
options: The output matches the schema’s shape, not that the content is right
You no longer need business-rule checks
questions.explanation: Constrained decoding controls shape. A well-formed order_id can still point at an order that doesn’t exist.
